items.followUp: Why are gases more compressible than liquids?

rubric.why: Identifies the greater separation of gas particles compared with liquid particles.
rubric.description: Gas particles are much farther apart than liquid particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that gas particles are far apart or have large spaces between them.

accept: less mass in a given volume
rubric.why: Connects the particle separation to lower mass per unit volume.
rubric.description: The same volume of gas contains less mass, so its density is lower.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that gas has less mass in the same volume or a lower density as a result.

modelAnswer: Gas particles are much farther apart than particles in a liquid.
Therefore, the same volume of gas contains less mass, so its density is lower.

items.followUp: Write the balanced chemical equation for the reaction of chlorine with cold, dilute sodium hydroxide.

rubric.why: Checks that the reactants and products are correctly identified.
rubric.description: Chlorine reacts with sodium hydroxide to form sodium chloride, sodium hypochlorite and water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including the correct reactants and products.

rubric.why: Checks that the chemical equation is balanced.
rubric.description: The balanced equation is 2NaOH + Cl₂ → NaCl + NaClO + H₂O.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the correctly balanced equation.

items.followUp: Write down any three differences between an element and a compound.

rubric.why: Distinguishes compounds from mixtures by how their substances are joined.
rubric.description: A compound is formed by chemical combination; a mixture is formed by physical mixing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating this distinction.

rubric.why: Identifies the fixed composition of compounds compared with the variable composition of mixtures.
rubric.description: A compound has a fixed composition; the proportions of substances in a mixture can vary.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating this distinction.

rubric.why: Contrasts the properties of compounds with those of the components of mixtures.
rubric.description: A compound has properties different from those of its constituent elements; mixture components retain their properties.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating this distinction.

rubric.why: Distinguishes how compounds and mixtures can be separated.
rubric.description: A compound is separated by chemical methods; a mixture can be separated by physical methods.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating this distinction.

rubric.why: Contrasts the definite formula of a compound with the absence of a definite formula for a mixture.
rubric.description: A compound has a definite chemical formula; a mixture has no definite chemical formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating this distinction.

modelAnswer: A compound is formed by chemical combination of elements; a mixture is formed by physical mixing of substances.
A compound has a fixed composition; the proportions of substances in a mixture can vary.
A compound has properties different from those of its constituent elements; the components of a mixture retain their properties.
A compound can be separated into its elements by chemical methods; the components of a mixture can be separated by physical methods.
A compound has a definite chemical formula; a mixture has no definite chemical formula.
